evidence: Receiving DO2 at t=48.0 h: 10.75 mg/L; at t=48.2 h: 2.43 mg/L — abrupt ~8 mg/L collapse
Receiving DO2 at t=52.0 h: 1.64 mg/L, below minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0
Source batches (source-1/2/3) DO2 at t=48–52 h remain ~10.5–11.2 mg/L, showing receiving-only abnormality
Receiving P assay (t=48 h, avail 52 h): 3.04 g/L — substantial product mass to retain; stop yields zero production
Source batches peak P ~8 g/L near 72–84 h, indicating substantial remaining production potential if DO constraint is resolved
Sensor series 48.2–52.0 h consistently 1.6–2.9 mg/L, ruling out single-point artifact
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~10.7 mg/L at t=48 h to ~2.4 mg/L and continues declining to 1.64 mg/L at the 52 h decision point, violating the 2.0 mg/L minimum oxygen constraint, while all three source batches at the same age hold ~10.5–11.2 mg/L. This indicates excess metabolic demand (likely over-feeding at the onset of the production phase). Product is already ~3 g/L (matching source trajectories at 48 h) with substantial remaining production potential (sources reach ~8 g/L by 72–84 h), so stopping would forfeit counted production. A 15% air increase alone is insufficient to overcome an ~8 mg/L demand gap; a mild 20% feed cut leaves DO at the constraint edge. The strong feed reduction (feed 0.6, air 1.15) maximizes DO recovery margin, retains all accumulated product mass, and keeps the fermentation productive once oxygen recovers.
args.uncertainty: Source and receiving processes differ; hidden receiving parameters are unobserved, so the cause of the DO crash (feed overdosing vs. mixing/aeration fault vs. contamination-like demand) cannot be confirmed. The demand–feed response magnitude is inferred from the size of the DO drop and source comparison, not from a calibrated receiving model. If the deficit is equipment-driven rather than feed-driven, feed reduction alone may be slow to restore DO above 2.0 mg/L and air capacity could bind; the intervention is bounded and reviewable, and continued monitoring is warranted.
